_comment: Generated by tools/verify_claims.py. Do not hand-edit: every value is re-derived from the measured file named in source_file. A number with no entry here is a number we are not allowed to publish.

claims.statement: Map-in-loop vs free dead reckoning, lower median POSITION ERROR (not drift %) across 43 real GNSS outages, vehicle CAN ground truth
claims.note: Quote as 2.02x lower median position error. The drift-% ratio is a different number (1.65x) and the two must never share a cell.

claims.statement: Free dead-reckoning median position error over the outage set
COAST median position error over the same outage set
Free dead-reckoning median drift as % of distance travelled
COAST median drift as % of distance travelled. ISRO bar is <10% -- we do NOT clear it, and say so first.
A PERFECT (oracle) yaw sensor still fails this share of 60 s segments. The negative result the pitch is built on.
Free-DR pass rate, ISRO short arm (<5 m over 50 m, <60 s)
Free-DR pass rate, ISRO tunnel arm (<10% and <100 m/km over 60 s)
Loosely-coupled GNSS+INS fusion vs GNSS alone. A WASH -- report it. The PS asks for an AI-based fusion model; ours is classical.

Post-hoc road snapping vs free dead reckoning. BELOW 1.0 -- snapping a drifted track onto a confidently wrong road makes it worse. This is the control that proves the value is in-loop, not in the map.

Worst measured edge-engine configuration (180-particle graph filter, 100% GNSS-denied, 200 Hz). Publish THIS, not a best case: it is 98x the 200 Hz requirement and cannot be attacked with a harder scenario.
Worst measured edge throughput as a multiple of the 200 Hz requirement
Best measured edge-engine configuration. Quote only with its configuration attached, never as the headline.
The km/h-vs-m/s loader bug we found in our OWN pipeline, which inflated every reported drift %. Historical, not a current measurement -- the resolver only confirms the write-up still documents it.
Phone compass heading error vs GPS course, after granting a perfect per-drive mount and declination offset. Lower bound on real error.
